citeinfo.othercit: This metadata record is a template for data created using the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) Digital Shoreline Analysis System (DSAS) version 6.2 application. Basic process steps and attribute fields have been described but MANY REQUIRED FIELDS HAVE BEEN LEFT BLANK in order for the DSAS user to enter their specifications. Therefore, this metadata file is not FGDC-compliant as is. DSAS version 6 is a desktop application that loads geospatial files (geoJSON or shapefile) saved by a Geographic Information System. The DSAS software requires users to import a reference baseline and a set of shoreline positions. DSAS will then generate measurement transects and shoreline intersections which it will use to calculate rate-of-change statistics. In addition, DSAS provides uncertainties associated with rates of change. This metadata file accompanies a rates file of the same name that was created using the Digital Shoreline Analysis System version 6.2.

attr.attrdef: The total cumulative distance (TCD) measures the distance along the baseline in meters from the start of the baseline segment with an ID=1 to the end of the last baseline segment.
The total number of shorelines intersected by the transect and used for change analysis.

A linear regression rate-of-change statistic was calculated by fitting a least-squares regression line to all shoreline points for a particular transect. The best-fit regression line is placed so that the sum of the squared residuals (determined by squaring the offset distance of each data point from the regression line and adding the squared residuals together) is minimized. The linear regression rate is the slope of the line. The rate is reported in meters per year with positive values indicating accretion and negative values indicating erosion. IF the Proxy Datum Bias (PDB) correction has been is applied, TWO versions of this statistic will be reported: "LRR" will include the PDB in the calculations; "NB_LRR" will not include the PDB. IF THE PROXY DATUM BIAS IS NOT USED, there will only be one value reported "LRR" which will not include a bias correction. A LRR value of 9999.99 in the attribute table means that value is Null. This scenario occurs when ShrCount = 2 and there are not enough data points to calculate a linear regression rate.

IF BIAS USED -The LRR without the Proxy Datum Bias applied.A 9999.99 in the attribute table means that value is Null. This scenario occurs when ShrCount = 2 and there are not enough data points to calculate a linear regression rate.

The R-squared statistic, or coefficient of determination, is the percentage of variance in the data that is explained by a regression. It is a dimensionless index that ranges from 1.0 to 0.0 and measures how successfully the best-fit line accounts for variation in the data. The smaller the variability of the residual values around the regression line relative to the overall variability, the better the prediction (and closer the R-squared value is to 1.0). IF the Proxy Datum Bias (PDB) correction has been is applied, TWO versions of this statistic will be reported: "LR2" will include the PDB in the calculations; "NB_LR2" will not include the PDB. IF THE PROXY DATUM BIAS IS NOT USED, there will only be one value reported "LR2" which will not include a bias correction. A LR2 value of 9999.99 in the attribute table means that LR2 is Null. This scenario occurs when ShrCount = 2 and there are not enough data points to calculate a linear regression rate.

The standard error of the slope with confidence interval describes the uncertainty of the reported rate for the user-selected confidence value captured as part of the attribute name. IF the Proxy Datum Bias (PDB) correction has been is applied, TWO versions of this statistic will be reported: "LCI90" will include the PDB; "NB_LCI90" will not include the PDB. IF THE PROXY DATUM BIAS IS NOT USED, there will only be one value reported "LCI90" which will not include a bias correction. An LCI90 value of 9999.99 in the attribute table means that LCI90 is Null. This scenario occurs when ShrCount = 2 and there are not enough data points to calculate a linear regression rate.

The standard error of a linear regression is the standard deviation of the residuals (the differences between the observed values and the values predicted by the model). A smaller standard error means the regression line fits the data more tightly; a larger one means the points are more scattered around the line. It indicates the typical error in the regression line’s prediction of shoreline position at a specific point in time. IF the Proxy Datum Bias (PDB) correction has been is applied, TWO versions of this statistic will be reported: "LSE" will include the PDB in the calculations; "NB_LSE" will not include the PDB. IF THE PROXY DATUM BIAS IS NOT USED, there will only be one value reported "LSE" which will not include a bias correction. A LSE value of 9999.99 in the attribute table means that LSE is Null. This scenario occurs when ShrCount = 2 and there are not enough data points to calculate a linear regression rate.

The end point rate (EPR) is calculated by determining the distance between the oldest and youngest shoreline on a DSAS transect and dividing by the time elapsed between the two shoreline dates. IF the Proxy Datum Bias (PDB) correction has been is applied, TWO versions of this statistic will be reported: "EPR" will include the PDB in the calculations; "NB_EPR" will not include the PDB. IF THE PROXY DATUM BIAS IS NOT USED, there will only be one value reported "EPR" which will not include a bias correction.

An estimate of end point rate uncertainty. The shoreline uncertainties for the two positions used in the end point calculation are each squared, then added together (summation of squares). The square root of the summation of squares is divided by the number of years between the two shorelines. IF the Proxy Datum Bias (PDB) correction has been is applied, TWO versions of this statistic will be reported: "EPRunc" will include the PDB in the calculations; "NB_EPRunc" will not include the PDB. IF THE PROXY DATUM BIAS IS NOT USED, there will only be one value reported "EPRunc" which will not include a bias correction.

Net shoreline movement (NSM)the distance between the oldest and youngest shorelines at each transect. IF the Proxy Datum Bias (PDB) correction has been is applied, TWO versions of this statistic will be reported: "NSM" will include the PDB in the calculations; "NB_NSM" will not include the PDB. IF THE PROXY DATUM BIAS IS NOT USED, there will only be one value reported "NSM" which will not include a bias correction.

Shoreline change envelope. The "SCE" value represents the greatest distance in meters among all the shorelines that intersect a given transect. The value for SCE is always positive. IF the Proxy Datum Bias (PDB) correction has been is applied, TWO versions of this statistic will be reported: "SCE" will include the PDB in the calculations; "NB_SCE" will not include the PDB. IF THE PROXY DATUM BIAS IS NOT USED, there will only be one value reported "SCE" which will not include a bias correction.

In a weighted linear regression (WLR), more reliable data are given greater emphasis or weight towards determining a best-fit line. In the computation of rate-of-change statistics for shorelines, greater emphasis is placed on data points for which the position uncertainty is smaller. IF the Proxy Datum Bias (PDB) correction has been is applied, TWO versions of this statistic will be reported: "WLR" will include the PDB; "NB_WLR" will not include the PDB. IF THE PROXY DATUM BIAS IS NOT USED, there will only be one value reported "WLR" which will not include a bias correction. A WLR value of 9999.99 in the attribute table means that value is Null. This scenario occurs when ShrCount = 2 and there are not enough data points to calculate a linear regression rate.

The R-squared statistic, or coefficient of determination, is the percentage of variance in the WLR that is explained by a regression.It is a dimensionless index that ranges from 1.0 to 0.0 and measures how successfully the best-fit line accounts for variation in the data. The smaller the variability of the residual values around the regression line relative to the overall variability, the better the prediction (and closer the R-squared value is to 1.0). IF the Proxy Datum Bias (PDB) correction has been is applied, TWO versions of this statistic will be reported: "WR2" will include the PDB; "NB_WR2" will not include the PDB. IF THE PROXY DATUM BIAS IS NOT USED, there will only be one value reported "WR2" which will not include a bias correction. A WR2 value of 9999.99 in the attribute table means that value is Null. This scenario occurs when ShrCount = 2 and there are not enough data points to calculate a linear regression rate.

The standard error of the slope with confidence interval describes the uncertainty of the reported rate for the user-selected confidence value captured as part of the attribute name. IF the Proxy Datum Bias (PDB) correction has been is applied, TWO versions of this statistic will be reported: "WCI90" will include the PDB; "NB_WCI90" will not include the PDB. IF THE PROXY DATUM BIAS IS NOT USED, there will only be one value reported "WCI90" which will not include a bias correction. A WCI90 value of 9999.99 in the attribute table means that value is Null. This scenario occurs when ShrCount = 2 and there are not enough data points to calculate a linear regression rate.

The standard error of the estimate for the weighted linear regression rate. The standard error evaluates the accuracy of the best-fit regression line (WLR) in predicting the position of a shoreline for a specific date. IF the Proxy Datum Bias (PDB) correction has been is applied, TWO versions of this statistic will be reported: "WSE" will include the PDB; "NB_WSE" will not include the PDB. overview.eaover: The entity and attribute information provided here describe the attributes that are generated using the Digital Shoreline Analysis System version 6 software. In some cases, the attributes described in this metadata file may not exist in the dataset. It is up to the DSAS user to verify the attributes and ensure all values are populated with regard to their dataset. In some cases attribute names will be capitalized within DSAS, but the exported version will have the same attribute names in lowercase.
